record.paper: Perfect shuffling with fewer lazy transpositions

dossier_meta.paper: Perfect shuffling with fewer lazy transpositions
dossier_meta.context_text: This generalises Problem 1 to the setting of shuffling $t$ distinguishable counters across $n$ positions using the fewest lazy transpositions. The upper bound $U_t(n)\leq tn-\binom{t+1}{2}$ is achieved by existing sweeping/divide-and-conquer constructions. When $t=n$ the problem reduces to Problem 1, which Theorem 2 answers negatively; the paper asks whether the trivial bound is tight for other values of $t$.
